title: One who has seen the supreme, And heard the unsurpassed, Gained the unsurpassed, Delights in the unsurpassed training, Established in service, Develops the specific recollections,…
content:
One who has seen the supreme,
And heard the unsurpassed,
Gained the unsurpassed,
Delights in the unsurpassed training,
Established in service,
Develops the specific recollections,
Connected to seclusion,
Attains security, the Deathless,
Joyful, not heedless,
Careful, guarding virtue,
When the time has ripened,
Suffering is destroyed.

title: - Just as a great crowd of people, bhikkhus, would gather together and say: 'The national beauty! The national beauty!' And that national beauty, with…
content: - Just as a great crowd of people, bhikkhus, would gather together and say: 'The national beauty! The national beauty!' And that national beauty, with all her charms, would dance for them, with all her charms, would sing for them. And an even larger crowd would gather and say: 'The national beauty dances and sings.' Then a man would come who wants to live, not to die, who wants happiness and loathes suffering. They would say to him: 'Friend, look here. This is a bowl filled with oil. You must carry this bowl of oil through the great crowd and the national beauty. And a man with a drawn sword will follow behind you. Wherever you spill even a little of the oil, there your head will fall.' What do you think, bhikkhus, would that man, not attending to the bowl of oil, let his mind wander outside?" - "Bhikkhus, I give this simile to convey the meaning. And this is the meaning: 'The bowl filled with oil' is a synonym for mindfulness of the body. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: 'We will develop mindfulness of the body, cultivate it, make it our vehicle, make it our base, establish it, accumulate it, and properly undertake it.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train.

title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in hell. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families,…
content: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in hell. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families, stinginess regarding gains, stinginess regarding praise, and causing donated goods to be wasted. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in hell. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in heaven. What five? No stinginess regarding dwellings, no stinginess regarding families, no stinginess regarding gains, no stinginess regarding praise, and not causing donated goods to be wasted. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in heaven.

title: - Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is my instruction to you. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful? Here, bhikkhus,…
content: - Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is my instruction to you. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world ... Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu clearly comprehending? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu knows feelings as they arise, knows feelings as they persist, knows feelings as they pass away; knows perceptions as they arise, knows perceptions as they persist, knows perceptions as they pass away. Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu clearly comprehending. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is my instruction to you.

title: Bhikkhus, if one does not intend, does not plan, but still has a tendency towards something, that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness.…
content: Bhikkhus, if one does not intend, does not plan, but still has a tendency towards something, that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, there is a support for the establishment of consciousness. When consciousness is established and grows, there is the production of future renewed existence. When there is future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering.

title: - What gives birth to a person? What always runs? What undergoes rebirth? Because of what is there no liberation? - Craving gives birth to…
content:
- What gives birth to a person?
What always runs?
What undergoes rebirth?
Because of what is there no liberation?
- Craving gives birth to a person,
The mind always runs,
Beings undergo rebirth,
Because of suffering, there is no liberation.

title: And, bhikkhus, when that bhikkhu has dwelt in these five things, four more things should be developed. The perception of foulness should be developed to…
content: And, bhikkhus, when that bhikkhu has dwelt in these five things, four more things should be developed. The perception of foulness should be developed to abandon greed; loving-kindness should be developed to abandon hatred; mindfulness of breathing should be developed to cut off thoughts; the perception of impermanence should be developed to uproot conceit. Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu with the perception of impermanence, the perception of non-self becomes established; for a bhikkhu with the perception of non-self, conceit is uprooted, and in this very life he attains Nibbāna.

title: For one who has no 'I' and 'mine' in regard to name-and-form, Who does not grieve over what is not, That one is truly called…
content:
For one who has no 'I' and 'mine' in regard to name-and-form,
Who does not grieve over what is not,
That one is truly called a bhikkhu.

A bhikkhu who dwells in loving-kindness,
With faith in the Buddha's teaching,
Attains the peaceful state,
The blissful state of peace.

Bhikkhu, empty this boat;
Empty, it will go quickly.
Having cut off greed and hatred,
You will go to Nibbāna.

title: Māluṅkyaputta, there are these four births of craving from which craving arises for a bhikkhu. What four? Either because of robes, Māluṅkyaputta, craving arises, from…
content: Māluṅkyaputta, there are these four births of craving from which craving arises for a bhikkhu. What four? Either because of robes, Māluṅkyaputta, craving arises, from which craving arises for a bhikkhu. Or because of almsfood... or because of lodging... or because of this or that kind of existence. Māluṅkyaputta, there are these four births of craving from which craving arises for a bhikkhu. When, Māluṅkyaputta, craving is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, unable to arise in the future — then, Māluṅkyaputta, that bhikkhu is called one who has destroyed craving, untied the fetters, rightly demolished conceit, and made an end of suffering.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, a lake that is clear, bright, not stirred up. A person with good eyes standing on the bank can see the oysters,…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, a lake that is clear, bright, not stirred up. A person with good eyes standing on the bank can see the oysters, the shells, the gravel, the pebbles, the schools of fish moving about and resting. Why is that? Because the water is not stirred up, bhikkhus. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu with a mind not stirred up can know his own benefit, can know the benefit of others, can know the benefit of both, can realize a superior human state, the truly noble distinction of knowledge and vision — this is possible. Why is that? Because the mind is not stirred up, bhikkhus.
